title: Is a diameter of a circle a line of symmetry?
description: A point on the rim of a circle is joined to the centre, and the segment is extended into a diameter. The circle is folded along that diameter and the two halves are compared. Keeko's doubt is that only the up and down diameter is a line of symmetry.
teaching_notes: One idea: folding a circle along any diameter makes the two halves overlap exactly. Watch for students who think only the vertical diameter works.

source: Take a point on the rim of a circle and join it to the centr
video_script.why: The child folds a circle along a diameter and sees that the halves overlap, then sees that every diameter does this.

final_answer.value: Yes. Every diameter of a circle is a line of symmetry

hold_back: Yes. Every diameter of a circle is a line of symmetry
maths_rules: a point on the rim joined to the centre and extended to the other side is a diameter
folding along the diameter makes the two halves overlap exactly
each point of one half lands on a point of the other half, at the same distance from the centre
the same holds for any point on the rim, so for every diameter
